function_question: How does nature let some visitors in and keep others out?

opening.text: There was a boy called Reza who loved the birds that visited his back garden. He knew the robin, the sparrows and the bossy blue tit by sight.
Reza filled his bird feeder with seeds before breakfast and watched from the window as the birds came to eat.
A clever squirrel found the feeder. It climbed the pole, hung upside down and gobbled every seed. "I don't want to hurt it," Reza said. "But the birds are hungry too!"

card.problem: A clever squirrel eats all the bird seed every day
card.goal: Design a feeder birds can use but a squirrel can't
card.rules: No hurting anyone: no grease, spikes, glue or spicy powder

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. A clever squirrel eats all the seed in Reza's bird feeder every day. Reza wants to keep it out without hurting it. Can you help him? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some designers already have a spark of an idea for outsmarting a squirrel. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature is full of clever doors that only let the right visitor in. Tap each card to meet four door keepers!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which surface will make the eraser slide at the lowest angle?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your feeder from the side, and show how a squirrel would try to get in!
guide.build_and_test: Build your feeder and run the squirrel test. How many minutes can you keep the pretend squirrel out?
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Find where the squirrel got in, change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Reza's garden is full of happy birds eating from a feeder like YOURS, and the squirrel has a nut corner of its own!

quick_check.question: A small bird weighs about 20 g. A squirrel weighs about 500 g. How many times heavier is the squirrel?
quick_check.right: Right! 500 ÷ 20 = 25. That's why a perch that sinks under a heavy weight can stop a squirrel but not a bird!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Divide the squirrel's weight by the bird's weight: 500 ÷ 20.

clue_cards.name: Pitcher plant
clue_cards.trick: Its rim gets super slippery when it's damp.
clue_cards.does: Insects skid on it and can't get a grip, like a car on a wet road.

clue_cards.name: Acacia
clue_cards.trick: It has thorns, and some kinds give ants a home inside them.
clue_cards.does: The thorns and ant guards keep leaf-eaters away.

clue_cards.name: Hummingbird flower
clue_cards.trick: It hides its nectar at the bottom of a long, thin tube.
clue_cards.does: Only a hummingbird's long beak can reach it.

clue_cards.name: Weaver bird
clue_cards.trick: Its nest hangs from a thin branch with the entrance at the bottom.
clue_cards.does: The bird flies straight in, but snakes struggle to get inside.

predict.prompt: Easy for a squirrel or hard for a squirrel? Predict first!

items.label: A feeder hanging from a tree branch
A wobbly, smooth dome above the feeder
A wide, smooth cone around the pole

predict.explain: Squirrels are brilliant climbers and jumpers, but they need something to grip. Smooth, round shapes that wobble or spin give their paws nothing to hold, while birds just fly around them.

lab.title: The slippery slope
lab.predict: Put an eraser on a board and slowly lift one end. On which surface will it start to slide at the lowest angle?
lab.measure: angle when it starts to slide (degrees)

tool.name: Empathy Map
tool.intro: An Empathy Map helps you understand the one you're designing for: what they say, think, do and feel. Today you have two users, the birds and the squirrel! Try one map for each.

parts.name: Says
parts.what: What does your user say out loud?
parts.example: 🎒 A student says: "My backpack hurts my shoulders."
parts.starter: If the squirrel could talk, it would say…

parts.name: Thinks
parts.what: What might they be thinking but not saying?
parts.example: 🎒 They think: "I wish I didn't have to carry every book."
parts.starter: The little birds might be thinking…

parts.name: Does
parts.what: What do you see them do?
parts.example: 🎒 They drag the backpack on one shoulder.
parts.starter: Every morning, the squirrel climbs up and…

parts.name: Feels
parts.example: 🎒 They feel tired and a bit grumpy by lunchtime.
parts.starter: When the feeder is empty, the birds feel…

sketch_checklist: I drew my feeder from the side with its pole or string.
I labelled the squirrel stopper and the bird door.
I showed that nothing on it can hurt a bird or a squirrel.

test.measure: minutes the 'squirrel test' fails to reach the seed
test.check_question: Bird check: can a pretend beak still reach the seed?

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped your feeder most?
